answered.sql: SELECT c.name, f.feature_name FROM Communities AS c JOIN Communities_Features AS cf ON c.id = cf.community_id JOIN Features AS f ON cf.feature_id = f.id

candidates.meaning: Show all features that are associated with any community.
candidates.sql: SELECT feature_name FROM Features WHERE id IN (SELECT feature_id FROM Communities_Features)

candidates.meaning: Show the names of communities and the features they have.
candidates.sql: SELECT C.name, F.feature_name FROM Communities AS C JOIN Communities_Features AS CF ON C.id = CF.community_id JOIN Features AS F ON CF.feature_id = F.id

candidates.meaning: List the unique features that are present in every community.
candidates.sql: SELECT feature_name FROM Features WHERE id IN (SELECT feature_id FROM Communities_Features GROUP BY feature_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT community_id) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Communities))

candidates.meaning: Display the features that are common to all communities.
candidates.sql: SELECT feature_name FROM Features WHERE id IN (SELECT feature_id FROM Communities_Features GROUP BY feature_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT community_id) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Communities))
